prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An automatic fiber stripping system comprises a first stripping module, a second stripping module, and a heating device. The first stripping module and the second stripping module each have a stripping belt, a driven belt wheel, a driving belt wheel, and a stripping tool including a pressing portion. The stripping belts are tightened on the pressing portions and the stripping tools press the stripping belts on each of two opposite sides of an optical cable. A blade portion of one of the stripping tools cuts a notch in at least one of two side edges of an outer coating layer of the optical cable. The heating device heats and softens the outer coating layer of the optical cable. The stripping belts are driven to move relative to the optical cable by the driving belt wheels so as to strip off a segment of the outer coating layer from the notch.

outputs.L2: An automated system for removing fiber coating includes a first stripping module, a second stripping module, and a heater. Each of the two stripping modules is provided with a stripping belt, a driven pulley, a drive pulley, and a stripping tool having a pressing section. The stripping belts are tensioned against the pressing sections, and the stripping tools force the belts against two opposing sides of an optical cable. outputs.L3:
The automatic fiber stripping system includes a first stripping module, a second stripping module, and a heating device. The first stripping module and the second stripping module are arranged to cooperate with each other so as to process an optical cable positioned between them.

Each stripping module includes a stripping belt, a plurality of belt wheels, and a stripping tool. The stripping belt is mounted around the belt wheels and is driven to move along a predetermined path. The stripping tool is arranged adjacent to the stripping belt and includes a pressing portion. During operation, the pressing portion of each stripping tool presses the corresponding stripping belt against the optical cable.

The first stripping module and the second stripping module are positioned on opposite sides of the optical cable. As a result, the stripping tools of the two stripping modules press the stripping belts against opposite side surfaces of the optical cable. This allows the optical cable to be firmly held and frictionally engaged by the moving stripping belts.

At least one of the stripping tools further includes a blade portion. The blade portion is configured to cut a notch in at least one side edge of an outer coating layer of the optical cable. The notch forms an initial opening or weakened region in the outer coating layer, thereby facilitating subsequent removal of the coating material.

The heating device is arranged to heat the optical cable, particularly the outer coating layer thereof. By applying heat, the heating device softens the outer coating layer and reduces the bonding force or mechanical strength of the coating material. After the notch has been formed and the outer coating layer has been softened, the stripping belts are driven to move relative to the optical cable. The movement of the stripping belts applies a stripping force to the softened outer coating layer, causing a segment of the outer coating layer to be peeled or stripped away from the notch.

In this manner, the automatic fiber stripping system can efficiently remove a desired segment of the outer coating layer of the optical cable. The cooperation of the blade portion, the heating device, and the moving stripping belts enables stable and automated stripping while reducing the risk of damage to the optical fiber inside the optical cable.
outputs.L4:
An automatic fiber stripping system is designed to remove the outer coating of an optical cable or optical fiber in a controlled and repeatable manner. The system includes two opposing stripping modules arranged on opposite sides of the cable. Each stripping module is provided with a driven stripping belt and at least one pressing stripping tool. During operation, the optical cable is positioned between the two modules, and the stripping tools press the cable coating against the moving belts.

Before the coating is removed, a blade is used to form a notch or cut in the outer coating at a predetermined stripping position. This notch defines the starting point for removal of the coating segment. A heating device may also be arranged near the stripping area to warm and soften the coating material. By softening the coating, the system reduces the force required for stripping and helps prevent damage to the optical fiber inside.

Once the notch has been formed and the coating has been sufficiently softened, the stripping belts are driven in a stripping direction. The belts grip the coating segment on both sides of the cable and move relative to the cable. As the belts advance, they peel the coating away from the notch and separate the coating segment from the underlying optical fiber. The opposing arrangement of the stripping modules helps apply balanced forces to the cable, improving stripping accuracy and reducing the risk of bending, breaking, or otherwise damaging the fiber.

This automated process allows the outer coating to be removed quickly, consistently, and with minimal manual handling. By combining cutting, heating, pressing, and belt-driven stripping actions, the system provides an efficient solution for preparing optical fibers for subsequent operations such as splicing, connector installation, inspection, or further processing.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article because it points to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book; we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

Although “the” may seem simple, it helps make sentences clearer and more precise. It can refer to something already mentioned, something unique, or something known by context. In phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” or “the answer,” the word gives focus and meaning.

Without “the,” English would sound less natural and often more confusing. This small word shows how even the simplest parts of language can have great importance. “The” may be short, but it is essential in everyday speech and writing.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent-style abstract for an automatic fiber stripping system with two belt-based stripping modules, stripping tools with pressing portions and a blade, and a heater that softens an optical cable coating before stripping it from a notch.
counterfactuals.output: An automatic fiber stripping system includes first and second belt-based stripping modules configured to engage and convey an optical cable. Each stripping module includes stripping tools having pressing portions for clamping the optical cable and a blade for forming or engaging a notch in a coating of the optical cable. A heater is positioned upstream of the stripping tools and configured to heat and soften the coating before stripping. After the coating is softened, the belt-based stripping modules drive the stripping tools relative to the optical cable to strip the coating from the notch, thereby exposing an optical fiber with reduced damage and improved stripping consistency.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention described here: an optical cable outer coating is heated, notched along a side edge by a stripping tool, and then removed by opposed moving stripping belts driven by belt wheels.

The first and second stripping modules are positioned so that respective stripping belt portions face one another across the optical cable, and corresponding stripping tools are configured to press the belt portions against opposite sides of the optical cable with a predetermined contact force. During operation, the driving wheels rotate the stripping belts in coordination with cable advancement or withdrawal, while the tools urge the belts into frictional engagement with the cable jacket or coating to abrade, cut, peel, or remove an outer layer of the optical cable.
